labelStatus: AI-authored design expectations; not independent human ground truth

cases.text: The route planner proposes a route. A dispatcher must approve each proposed route before the planner executes it; rejected routes are never executed.
The grant assistant cannot execute a recommendation until a human reviewer signs its individual approval record. This is required for every recommendation.
Every stock-transfer recommendation waits for a warehouse supervisor's approval. The stock planner executes a transfer only after that approval.
The delivery assistant executes every proposed action without asking anyone to approve it. There is no prior approval step.
The notification assistant executes recommendations immediately. Human reviewers receive a report afterward, but never approve recommendations before execution.
Low-value recommendations execute without human approval; all others require approval. The allocation assistant uses this rule in production.
People remain in charge of the study helper. Its documentation does not explain how this control works.
A reviewer endorses each queue-helper proposal before it leaves the holding area. The document does not say whether leaving that area is before or after execution.
Every recommendation requires approval before execution. The same assistant executes all recommendations immediately without waiting for approval. Both statements describe the same deployment.
The table assistant produces monthly summary tables from fictional amounts and dates. Tables have four columns.
A human reviews the spelling of the assistant's user manual. This review does not concern recommendations or their execution.
Reviewers approve labels in the assistant's synthetic training dataset. The paragraph describes dataset preparation only, not approval of deployed recommendations.
